text:
Emma - Support: Heads up — multiple customers reporting 503s to the /v1/generate hosted endpoint starting ~12:34 UTC after the last canary. High priority, billing team pinged. :warning:
Raj - Oncall SRE: On it. Any customer IDs or sample request IDs?
Emma - Support: Customer A sent request_id=req_9f2a. Also seeing a cluster of errors in sentry: "upstream 503 ServiceUnavailable" and some timeouts.
Carlos - Platform: Deploy bot shows a canary flip at 12:30:24 UTC. deploy-bot: "deploy started: canary/model-serving:v3.4.2 -> 12:30:24"
Mike - Deploy: That canary had a config key change: feature_route_ratio = 0.15 -> 0.5 (seed traffic bump). Could be hitting a path we didn't exercise.
Raj - Oncall SRE: Ok running quick smoke. curl -v 'https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"input":"hello"}'
Emma - Support: Repro from our side shows intermittent 503s (~1/6 requests) and 2-3s connection attempts then 503.
Raj - Oncall SRE: Pulling gateway logs for canary-tagged instances... snippet: 
```
[12:31:12] upstream-response: 502
[12:31:13] heap-alloc: 92% (canary-07)
[12:31:14] upstream-response: 503
[12:31:15] request-id=req_9f2a latency=0ms backend=canary-07 error="cache-miss-retry-failed"
```
Carlos - Platform: heap pressure on canary nodes looks real — a memory leak in the new kernel-path branch we didn't catch in canary smoke. OOMs causing proxy to reject with 503.
Mike - Deploy: Rolling the canary back to v3.4.1 now. deploy-bot: "rollout: canary rollback to model-serving:v3.4.1 initiated by @Mike at 12:38:03"
Raj - Oncall SRE: Setting routing fallback to stable for affected region: `set-route-weight --env=prod --route=/v1/generate --stable=1.0` (will force 100% to stable).
Emma - Support: Notifying Customer A with ETA for mitigation. Billing flagged potential impact to invoiced tokens. billing-bot: "impact detected: customers affected=4, estimated missed requests ~1200"
Carlos - Platform: Also observed a config flag typo in the new canary: `kvcache.prefetch.window=0` got deployed (should be 200). That plus the kernel change explains the cache thrash and mem pressure.
Raj - Oncall SRE: Good catch. Steps I'm taking: 1) keep rollback in progress, 2) drain canary instances, 3) run heap-profiling on a retained replica, 4) bump prefetch to 200 in next patch and re-run canary smoke with load generator.
Mike - Deploy: Rollback completed at 12:42:10 according to deploy-bot. Canaries draining. deploy-bot: "rollback complete: canary v3.4.1 at 12:42:10"
Emma - Support: Customers reporting errors dropping back to baseline. Sending follow-up message to impacted accounts and opening refunds/credits as needed.
Raj - Oncall SRE: Leaving this thread open until we verify no residual 5xx spikes for 30m and new patch baked. Also filing a postmortem ticket: INF-2942.
Carlos - Platform: Will open a PR to add a pre-deploy validation that rejects kvcache.prefetch.window=0 for this model-serving path and add a memory regression test to the canary job.
Emma - Support: Thanks all — will update support ticket and close once monitoring window clears. :thumbsup:
Mike - Deploy: Quick timeline for PMs: canary flip at 12:30, 503 spike noticed by 12:34, rollback initiated 12:38, rollback complete 12:42, errors back to baseline by 12:45.
Raj - Oncall SRE: Adding monitoring dashboards and a canary-runbook note: if mem% > 85% and 5xx rate > 1% within 5 minutes, auto-weight back to stable.
Emma - Support: Closing loop with billing — will reconcile credits with infra after postmortem.
